question: On the WHO partograph, the action line is drawn 4 hours to the right of the alert line, and crossing the action line mandates immediate intervention.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. This statement is true. The two-line partograph places the action line exactly 4 hours right of the alert line. Crossing the alert line prompts increased vigilance; crossing the action line demands immediate intervention.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The alert line begins at 4 cm cervical dilatation and progresses at 1 cm/hour. The action line is drawn 4 hours to its right. Crossing the action line requires immediate obstetric review and a management decision (augmentation, operative delivery, or transfer).
